top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a distinct, mature and reproducible advance: the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, in which the lattice light shift cancels by design so many atoms can be interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free. It has reached 10^-18 uncertainty across independent laboratories and species (Sr, Yb, Hg) and is now used for redshift, varying-constant and dark-matter tests. The Katori and Ye allocation is the cleanest on the slate, and the citation scope is separated from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock prizes. P002 is a sound, mature theory with experimental checks, but it overlaps the 2016 prize concept and has narrow support; I rank it above no award because it is a legitimate achievement, and I defer to colleagues on soft-matter physics.
recusal_note: No direct conflict with Katori or Ye apparent from profile; as WACQT director and a superconducting-circuits theorist I have no stake in the clock or hexatic proposals, though my field-adjacent AMO colleagues are not close collaborators.
